name: Commercial API LLMs used zero-/few-shot (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini) as direct predictor, teacher / pseudo-labeler, or ensemble member
links: Anthropic API docs (docs.anthropic.com / platform.claude.com, Messages + Message Batches + prompt caching); OpenAI API docs (platform.openai.com, Responses/Chat Completions, Batch API, logprobs for non-reasoning models); Google Gemini API docs (ai.google.dev, responseLogprobs, batch mode); task README (github.com/ilopezgazpio/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI) explicitly allows API-based and prompted systems; reversal-curse background: Berglund et al. ICLR 2024 (arXiv:2309.12288); LLM NLI hallucination/bias: McKenna et al. 2023 'Sources of Hallucination by LLMs on Inference Tasks' (Findings EMNLP); consistency correction: Mitchell et al. 2022 ConCoRD (arXiv:2211.11875); pilot paper: aclanthology.org/2026.lrec-1.423 (states proprietary models were not evaluated).
year: Continuously updated; current generation at the time of writing (Sep 2026) includes Claude Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5 family, OpenAI GPT-5.x / GPT-6 family, Google Gemini 3.x family [uncertain]
license_access: Closed weights, commercial API access (pay per token; usage policies; data-retention terms). For the shared task the system must be disclosed as commercial/API-based (or hybrid if combined with open models). Model versions change over time, so pin dated model ids and cache all outputs for reproducibility.
track_coverage: All four tracks (T1 EN, T2 ES, T3 EU, T4 mixed) with no training. Frontier API models are the strongest available Basque-capable systems, so relative value is highest on T3 and T4.
basque_quality: Frontier API models are widely reported to handle Basque well (HiTZ's Latxa work used GPT-4-class models as strong Basque reference points; GPT-4-class models outperformed open 7-70B models on Basque benchmarks such as EusExams/EusProficiency/BertaQA-eu) [uncertain on exact numbers]. The organisers also mention selected translation-capable LLMs among the systems used to draft ES/EU data, implying adequate Basque generation quality. No published phrase-level NLI number in Basque exists for these models [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: Expected to be the most language-robust option: frontier LLMs reason in a largely language-agnostic way, so the en-eu / es-eu mixed views should lose only a few points relative to monolingual EN [uncertain]. The prompt can also ask the model to internally translate both phrases to English before judging. Main residual risk is translation artefacts in the ES/EU data (a Basque phrase whose translation drifts in specificity), which affect all systems equally.
architecture: Decoder-only (dense or MoE) instruction-/RL-tuned LLMs, many with optional extended reasoning. Used via prompting: (a) row-level prompt 'Given phrase A and phrase B, choose EQUIVALENCE / FORWARD_ENTAILMENT (A entails B) / BACKWARD_ENTAILMENT (B entails A) / NEGATIVE_OTHER' with the PhrasIS/iSTS annotation conventions and k-shot examples retrieved from train by similarity; (b) pair-level prompt that shows the unordered pair once and asks for the relation in a canonical frame, then maps it to both ordered rows via Rev (consistent by construction); (c) teacher mode: label new/augmented phrase pairs (translations, iSTS chunk pairs, synthetic minimal pairs) in both orders and keep only reverse-consistent outputs for student fine-tuning. Structured outputs (JSON schema / tool call) constrain the label set.
params: Undisclosed (closed models; frontier models are believed to be hundreds of billions to trillions of parameters, often MoE).
compute: No local GPU needed; runs from the local machine via API. Throughput limited by rate limits; batch APIs (Anthropic Message Batches, OpenAI Batch, Gemini batch) give ~50% discount and finish within 24h. Prompt caching of the long instruction + few-shot block cuts input cost substantially.
sample_efficiency: Uses the ~1.3k reversible source pairs only as few-shot pool and prompt-tuning dev set, so no overfitting from training; the danger is instead over-tuning the prompt on dev. Variance comes from sampling (use temperature 0 or majority vote over k samples) and model-version drift. Few-shot retrieval (kNN over train by phrase embedding) is the main lever for teaching PhrasIS-specific conventions (e.g. '22 dead' vs '89 dead' annotated as BACKWARD_ENTAILMENT, numerals, public figures, prepositional chunks).
reported_results: No DiCo-NLI or PhrasIS results for API models (the pilot explicitly did not evaluate proprietary models). Related evidence: GPT-4-class models reach ~85-90% on MNLI/SNLI-style NLI zero/few-shot but typically trail fine-tuned encoders on dataset-specific annotation conventions [uncertain]; GPT-4 3-shot was the strongest system in a news factual-entailment study (0.80 accuracy, 0.65 macro-F1, arXiv:2406.16842); LLMs are known to show attestation and relative-frequency biases in entailment (McKenna et al. 2023) and to be imperfectly consistent under reformulation / argument swaps (recent frontier models ~87% family consistency in a 2026 controlled-reformulation study, arXiv:2607.14528 [uncertain]). Zero-shot small open LLMs on XNLI-eu are only 0.40-0.48 (arXiv:2504.03312), while frontier API models are far stronger in Basque. Expected zero/few-shot DiCo weighted F1 is in the 0.60-0.75 range for T1 [uncertain], i.e. likely below a fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 (pilot 0.75) because of annotation-convention mismatch, but potentially above fine-tuned multilingual encoders on T3.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot; the authors list 'we do not evaluate large proprietary models' as a limitation. Pilot best results for reference: DeBERTa-v3-base Positives-A F1 0.75, unseen SoftCoh 0.84, unseen HardCoh 0.79.
consistency_guarantee: none for independent row-level prompting (the pilot and reversal-curse literature suggest order sensitivity); architectural (by construction) when using the pair-level canonical-frame prompt that emits one relation per unordered pair; inference-time if row-level outputs are combined via joint decoding.
negative_other_handling: NEGATIVE_OTHER must be defined in the prompt as the catch-all for PhrasIS opposition / similar / related / unrelated relations. LLMs tend to over-use 'related but not entailed' categories or, conversely, to be generous with entailment on near-synonyms; calibration of the NEG boundary with few-shot examples and dev-set threshold tuning (if probabilities available) is needed. With row-level prompts it can emit NEG on one direction and FE/BE on the other (costing SoftCons); the pair-level prompt emits NEG for both rows or none.
metric_tradeoff: Pair-level prompting gives SoftCons = 1.0 on all pairs where a non-NEG relation is predicted and HardCons equal to pair accuracy; Weighted F1 likely below the best fine-tuned encoder on T1/T2 due to annotation-convention mismatch, but potentially competitive or better on T3/T4. As an ensemble member or teacher it mostly helps Weighted F1 on hard lexico-semantic/world-knowledge cases (the pilot's dominant error types).
integration: Standalone script (not an HF model): build prompts from the participant CSVs, call the API with structured JSON output, cache raw responses to disk keyed by (model_id, prompt hash, instance_id), and convert them to 4-way probability vectors in src/labels.py LABELS order (from logprobs when available, else from k-sample vote frequencies or a verbalised confidence, smoothed). Plug these vectors into joint decoding / view pooling / stacking alongside fine-tuned models; for distillation, write pseudo-labelled pairs as extra training CSV rows in the same schema.
ensemble_compatibility: Partially. OpenAI (non-reasoning models) and Gemini expose token logprobs; Anthropic Claude does not expose logprobs, and reasoning-mode models generally do not either [uncertain]. Workable substitutes: k-sample vote frequencies (k=5-10 at temperature ~0.7) or asking for a per-label probability distribution; these are coarse and need calibration on dev before pooling.
inference_cost: Test size ~660 rows per monolingual track and ~4k rows for T4 (assuming dev-like proportions), i.e. ~6k rows or ~3k unordered pair-views. With a ~1.5k-token cached prompt and ~20-50 output tokens per call, one full pass with a frontier model costs roughly USD 5-40 (less with batch discounts and pair-level prompting; more with extended reasoning or k-sample voting) and runs in minutes to hours depending on rate limits [uncertain]. Pseudo-labelling 10-50k extra pairs would cost roughly USD 50-500 [uncertain].
rules_disclosure: Must disclose access regime = commercial/API-based (or hybrid/ensemble if combined with open-weight models), architecture family = decoder-only (closed), prompt engineering, and any external data; all prompts and model versions must be documented in the system paper. Allowed by the README ('Open-weight, API-based, fine-tuned, prompted, and hybrid systems are allowed unless the final task rules introduce a specific restriction'). Risks: final rules could restrict API use or require separate reporting; reproducibility concerns with deprecated model versions; provider terms may restrict using outputs to train competing models (distillation) - check each provider's terms before using outputs as training data for a released model [uncertain]. Using a distilled open student still requires disclosing the API teacher.
contamination: Highest contamination exposure of all options: frontier models are trained on web-scale data up to 2025-2026 that very likely includes the public iSTS 2015/2016 releases and possibly the PhrasIS repository (2024) and the task's public GitHub trial/train/dev files (released Sep 2026, likely after training cutoffs for current models) [uncertain]. Memorised PhrasIS labels could inflate test performance if DiCo test pairs come from public PhrasIS items; the task paper may ask for this to be discussed. The organisers also used translation-capable LLMs to draft ES/EU data, so API models may find the translations stylistically familiar.
structural_cue_dependence: None for row-level prompting. Pair-level prompting needs twin identification (derivable from instance_id or by matching swapped texts); if test metadata changes, fall back to row-level prompting plus text-based twin matching.
expected_gain: Most valuable as (1) a teacher/pseudo-labeler to expand the tiny training set (translate-train augmentation, new phrase pairs) with reverse-consistency filtering, and (2) a diverse ensemble member for T3/T4 where open models are weakest in Basque; plausible +1-4 Weighted F1 in ensembles and larger gains on EU [uncertain]. As a standalone predictor it is unlikely to beat fine-tuned encoders on T1/T2 because PhrasIS annotation conventions are idiosyncratic. Cheap to try (tens of dollars), so a quick few-shot dev evaluation early is worthwhile; the pair-level canonical prompt gives SoftCons = 1.0 for free.
